programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo's post-war exploration of Merseyside to Teesside finds him in York, a paradise for rail enthusiasts. Michael also takes the driver's seat in an Intercity 125, which propelled Britain into the age of high-speed rail

programme.title: Wainwright Walks

programme.title: The Treasures of Ancient Rome
programme.desc: Alastair Sooke reveals how the Romans' obsession with sex and violence was reflected in their art, and dons a wetsuit to visit the remains of emperor Claudius's pleasure palace. He also examines the bombastic pieces the Empire has become renowned for, including monumental arches and columns whose imagery relays the story of glorious military victories. Plus, the story of the emperor Hadrian, who redesigned the Pantheon in Rome

programme.title: Mary Beard Remembers - Ultimate Rome: Empire Without Limit

She explains how the programme wasn't just an education for her in regard to the Roman Empire, but also provided her with some valuable lessons in the art of film-making. Plus, Mary reveals some behind-the-scenes stories that will add new context for viewers

programme.title: Mary Beard's Ultimate Rome: Empire Without Limit

In the first edition, she gains an insight into the deep-rooted psyche of the people of Rome, looks at the expansion of the city, and travels to Greece, where Rome adopted a complex mix of brute force and cultural cringe, and France, where she finds evidence of war methods akin to genocide

programme.desc: The actor explores some of the most important archaeological finds in Ireland's history, revealing how many have been used as an important tool for nation-building on both sides of the border. Speaking to world-renowned experts, he unravels a forgotten time period, when a team of Americans from Harvard University, a Nazi archaeologist from Austria, and a Welsh geography professor dug up ancient sites across the country. Their pioneering work answered questions about the Celts, and what it means to be Irish

programme.title: Kamikaze: An Untold History
programme.desc: On the Pacific front, towards the end of the Second World War, Japan's imperial armed forces launched kamikaze attacks - suicide missions by aircraft laden with bombs. Close to 4,000 Japanese airmen died, and nearly 7,000 Allied military personnel were killed, and thousands more were injured by the attacks. How could this happen? Utilising 15 years' worth of extensive interviews with US and Japanese veterans, Takayuki Oshima's film delves into the mechanism of how a crazed madness swept through an entire nation

programme.title: The Sky at Night

programme.title: The Wildest Weather in the Universe: Horizon
programme.desc: Documentary following scientists conducting research into weather on other planets, using unmanned spacecraft to study the solar system and the latest telescopes to examine distant worlds. Their findings have revealed strange phenomena including rains of precious stones, supersonic winds, storms that encompass entire worlds, and temperatures so hot that the clouds are formed of lava

programme.title: Beautiful Equations

programme.desc: Reports from BBC newsrooms across the country with analysis and discussion on the big stories of the day

programme.title: Scotland's Home of the Year 2024
programme.desc: Judges Anna Campbell-Jones, Banjo Beale and Danny Campbell visit properties in the south. They must choose between a self-build near Lockerbie, a stone cottage in Moffat which dates back to the 1700s, and an old manse in South Lanarkshire

programme.title: Island Crossings
programme.desc: The 35-year-old ferry MV Isle of Mull is taken to dry dock for its annual overhaul, and at the projected cost of 2.8 million it is the biggest planned spend on any ship in CalMac's history. Meanwhile it is changeover day on Iona, where the community welcomes different volunteers and religious groups to the island to pray, eat and work together in what they call 'radical hospitality'

programme.title: David Wilson's Crime Files
programme.desc: The criminologist reinvestigates Scotland's most notorious miscarriages of justice, and is joined by journalist Fiona Walker to look for the reasons they occur

programme.title: River City
programme.desc: Mulvaney is left desolate when his attempt to help Francis has dire consequences. Caitlin briefly considers putting a stop to her campaign against Scarlett. Tommy ends up in Callum's firing line and Eddie has a revelation for Tyler

programme.title: Icons of Football
programme.desc: More stories of how Scottish football's biggest stars made their names on and off the pitch, beginning with former Celtic, Barcelona and Sweden striker Henrik Larsson. He reflects on his upbringing in the city of Helsingborg and early promise at Hgaborg and Helsingborgs, and his difficult years at Feyenoord, where game time and confidence wavered. The programme charts his transformation at Celtic, where he became the defining player of an era, before his story as a player culminated in Spain, where he joined Barcelona and played a decisive role in their 2006 Champions League triumph. With contributions by Martin O'Neill, Chris Sutton, Johan Mjllby, Paul Lambert and Regi Blinker

programme.title: Scotcast
programme.desc: Discussion on Scotland's biggest news stories, with Martin Geissler, Laura Miller and Natalie Higgins

programme.title: Des Doesn't Do - Winter Sports
programme.desc: Des Clarke faces his aversion to winter sports with the help of TV presenter and Deacon Blue drummer Dougie Vipond. He tries to beat a snowy, slippy slope during a skiing lesson, is bossed about in a curling lesson by an MBE Olympic champion, and finally attempts to show that he's the boss of an unruly pack of Siberian huskies in a dog sledding lesson

programme.title: Reporting Scotland: News at Seven
programme.desc: Reports from BBC newsrooms across the country with analysis and discussion on the big stories of the day

programme.title: Sportscene: Championship Live
programme.desc: Partick Thistle v Livingston (Kick-off 7.30pm). All the action from the match at Wyre Stadium at Firhill. Partick narrowly missed out on promotion to the Premiership last term after losing to St Mirren in the play-off final, while Livingston were relegated from the top flight, so both sides will be expecting to be among the leading contenders for the title this time around

programme.title: Best of Only an Excuse?
programme.desc: A selection of sketches picked from the archives of the hit comedy, mixing classic characters, favourite skits and hilarious media spoofs. Frankie Boy rocks up at the petrol station, King Kenny dispenses managerial advice on the golf course and Sir Fergie lectures on leadership at Harvard. Starring Jonathan Watson, with Tony Roper, Mark Cox, Joy McAvoy, Grant Smeaton, Alistair McGowan and Kirsty Wark

programme.title: Still Game
programme.desc: The old friends have got themselves a set of wheels, but the open road turns into a highway to hell for Victor when Jack forces him to do all the driving. Sitcom, starring Ford Kiernan and Greg Hemphill

programme.title: Two Doors Down
programme.desc: Colin turns to his neighbours for support when he is unceremoniously dumped by Cathy. Beth and Eric do their best to cheer him up, but conversation is already strained when Christine turns up and demands all of the juicy details from the break up. Later, Ian and Gordon arrive to share some good news, and together the neighbours try their best to make Colin feel positive about his future as a single man

programme.title: Rip It Up
programme.desc: The evolution of the Scottish music industry and the bands that helped nurture it and still support it today. Featured artists include King Creosote, James Yorkston, Mogwai, Arab Strap, Teenage Fanclub, the Vaselines, the Pastels, and the Delgados

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: It's harvest time for Andy and Jo in Fife as they finally reap what they have down - and after a challenging year it remains to be seen what the wet weather might have cost them. Nick and Holly diversify with a new cattle venture in Dumfries, and the Bakers on Papa Westray take delivery of a milking cow and calf to add to their ever-growing family

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Brian Cunningham's beginner's guide to vegetable growing started in April, and now it's time to reap the rewards as he starts to harvest from the veg plot. Calum Clunie starts the sowing cycle again in his family sized plot as he sows for winter crops

programme.title: Paramedics on Scene
programme.desc: In Glasgow, Paul and Ryan of the Special Operations Response Team are called to a siege in a flat, where a man has barricaded himself inside and is threatening to harm himself. Meanwhile, Aberdeen-based crewmates Kirsty and Bruce are called to see Rebecca, who has suffered a severe anaphylactic attack, but she shows little sign of improvement after several doses of adrenaline, prompting a rapid journey on blue-lights to Aberdeen Royal Infirmary

programme.title: Reporting Scotland: News at Seven
programme.desc: Reports from BBC newsrooms across the country with analysis and discussion on the big stories of the day

programme.title: My Kind of Town
programme.desc: Ian Hamilton and his dog Major head to Cupar in Fife, a traditional market town that now has ambitions to be a digital hub. Ian gets the chance to practise his swing on the Kingarrock Hickory golf course and samples some tasty morsels at the farmers' market

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: The autumn sales are over and preparations are being made for winter. In Newtonmore in Cairngorms National Park, Robert MacKenzie needs to gather in all his cows back down to the croft for pregnancy testing, while on North Uist, the MacDonalds are harvesting potatoes grown in the sandy machair soil unique to the west of Scotland

programme.title: Murder Trial: Death of a Dog Walker
programme.desc: Part one of two. Former gamekeeper David Campbell stands accused of the premeditated murder of Brian Low, a 65-year-old groundsman on the same estate where they both worked. With the site of the murder exposed to the elements for days, police are unable to forensically link anyone to the deceased, so the prosecution build a case against the accused around smaller, individual strands of circumstantial evidence, while working to convince the jury that he's guilty beyond reasonable doubt

programme.title: David Wilson's Crime Files
programme.desc: The criminologist discusses the use of forensic science in crime detection, looking at its 19th-century origins and more recent use in unresolved murder cases that are decades old

programme.title: Scotcast
programme.desc: Discussion on Scotland's biggest news stories, with Martin Geissler, Laura Miller and Natalie Higgins

programme.title: Icons of Football
programme.desc: A profile of former Celtic, Barcelona and Sweden striker Henrik Larsson, who reflects on his upbringing in the city of Helsingborg and early promise at Hgaborg and Helsingborgs, and his difficult years at Feyenoord, where game time and confidence wavered. The programme charts his transformation at Celtic, where he became the defining player of an era, before his story as a player culminated in Spain, where he joined Barcelona and played a decisive role in their 2006 Champions League triumph. With contributions by Martin O'Neill, Chris Sutton, Johan Mjllby, Paul Lambert and Regi Blinker

programme.title: The Catch Up
programme.desc: A round-up of the day's news

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve Backshall explores the Indian Ocean, searching for an underwater giant that can weigh as much as a double-decker bus, and trying to spot the world's fastest fish

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve Backshall visits South Africa, where he swims with 30 blacktip sharks, examines a nest of killer bees and encounters a black eagle

programme.title: Live Tennis
programme.desc: The Canadian Open. Coverage from day four of the ATP 1000 event in Montreal and the WTA 1000 event in Toronto, both of which are hard-court tournaments, where the second round is scheduled to conclude. There was disappointment for Great Britain's Cameron Norrie at this stage last year as he was eliminated 3-6 7-6 3-6 by Australian Aleksandar Vukic, but Emma Raducanu guaranteed there would be one Brit in round three as she dispatched the number 32 seed Peyton Stearns in a 6-2 6-4 victory. The women's number one seed Coco Gauff was made to work hard for her place in the next round as she battled past Danielle Collins 7-5 4-6 7-6, while the men's top seed Alexander Zverev triumphed 7-6 6-4 over Adam Walton

programme.desc: Kilmarnock v Celtic (Kick-off 1.30pm). Coverage of the Scottish Premiership match from The BBSP Stadium Rugby Park. The most recent of those matches in February looked to be going in favour of the hosts when Tyreece John-Jules and Joe Hugill gave Kilmarnock a 2-0 lead at half-time, only for Sebastian Tounekti, Benjamin Nygren, and Julian Araujo to turn things around and give Martin O'Neill a victory in his 300th game in charge of the Glasgow club
